dsh-server-resources
See what is eating your machine — without leaving DeepSeek Harness.
Live CPU, RAM, swap and disk on Linux, macOS and Windows, with a ranked list of the biggest consumer
RAM, swap and disk on Linux, macOS and Windows, with a ranked list of the biggest consumers of each.
## Why
"The machine is slow" is a question, not an answer. This plugin adds a **Resources** tab to the DSH
right sidebar that answers the follow-ups in one place:

- *Is it CPU, memory, swap or disk?*
- *Which program is responsible — and how many copies of it are

running?*
- *What is actually filling the disk?*
No SSH session, no `htop`, no Activity Monitor, no Task Manager, no `ncdu`, no extra service to inst
SH session, no `htop`, no Activity Monitor, no Task Manager, no `ncdu`, no extra service to install.

The bundle patch it applies is `cordis.patch.yml`: one `insert` row named `server-resources`.
### What it needs from the OS
| OS | Needs | Notes |
| Linux | `/proc`, `df`, `du`, `find`, `ionice`, `getconf` | All present on any distro; BusyBox/Alpi

ne work too (no PSI on old kernels). |
| macOS | `sysctl`, `vm_stat`, `ps`, `df`, `mount` | Ships wi

th macOS. Tested on macOS 26 (Apple silicon). |
| Windows | PowerShell — `pwsh` (7+) or the built-in
`powershell.exe` (5.1) | Prefers `pwsh`: it starts ~15× faster. Tested on Windows Server 2025. |
## Safe by design

- **Read-only.** It never kills a process, deletes a file or changes a setting.
- **No dependencies,
no network.** Linux reads `/proc`; macOS runs `sysctl`/`vm_stat`/`ps`/`df`; Windows runs **one** Po
werShell script that only calls `Get-CimInstance`. Commands are started with a fixed argument list (
never a shell string), and the PowerShell script is sent with `-EncodedCommand`, so nothing from the

browser is ever interpolated into it.
- **Gentle on the machine.** Linux and macOS disk scans run a
t the lowest priority (`ionice -c3 nice -n19` / `nice -n19`); Windows uses a built-in walker that yi
elds to the event loop. All scans run one at a time, with a 150 s limit, a 5 min cache and at most 4
queued (the rest get HTTP 429). The overview is sampled at most once per second (more slowly on Win
dows) however many tabs are open, every command has a hard timeout so a dead network mount cannot ha

ng the panel, and polling stops while the tab is hidden.
- **Guarded paths.** `/proc`, `/sys`, `/dev
` and `/run` cannot be scanned on Linux/macOS; on Windows only drive-letter paths (`C:\…`) are accep
ted — UNC and `\\?\` paths are refused; every path goes through `realpath` and must be an existing d
irectory; the walker never follows symlinks or junctions, never leaves the volume it started on and

counts a hard link once.
[该节后续省略]
## Limitations

- **Numbers describe the host** DSH runs on; container (cgroup) limits are not shown.
- **macOS:** p
er-process CPU is macOS's own decaying average (it lags a sudden spike); swap is "none" until macOS

actually needs it; no per-process swap.
- **Windows:** one sample takes ~1–2 s (PowerShell + CIM), s
o the panel refreshes every few seconds instead of 2.5 s; "System Idle Process" is left out of the C
PU ranking; processes of other users are listed but may lack a command line without administrator ri
ghts. Antivirus/EDR products sometimes flag any repeated `powershell -EncodedCommand`; the plugin av
oids `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` and starts PowerShell by absolute path to look as ordinary as possibl

e, but if your policy blocks it the panel says so instead of showing zeros.
- **Unreadable folders:*
* on macOS (Full Disk Access / TCC) and Windows (protected system folders) some folders cannot be re
ad without elevated rights; the Disk tab counts them ("N folders could not be read") instead of sile

ntly under-reporting.
- If `/proc` is mounted with `hidepid` (Linux), processes of other users are n

ot readable; the tab shows how many were skipped.
- Disk scans of very large trees stop after 2.5 mi
n and return a partial result (clearly marked). On Windows the built-in walker is ~5–15× slower than

`du` (a 5 GB tree takes a few seconds).
- Not supported: BSDs, Android, 32-bit Windows. On those th
e tab shows a clear "unsupported platform" message.
